# Original full-width atomic flag consumer

This self-authored, header-free C11 function updates one atomic DWORD status word. It discards the old result of each OR, AND and XOR, atomically loads the word after each update, and returns the XOR checksum of those three observations. Every operation uses sequentially consistent source ordering. The masks contain multiple bits and require full DWORD literals.

The discovery source and fixed producer profile were preserved before execution. Root ran two fresh builds with the unchanged i686 freestanding profile. Both produced the same 533-byte source, 556-byte ordinary i386 COFF object, complete 36-byte function and 863-byte Intel disassembly. The observed function contains three seven-byte LOCK 81 memory instructions: OR at offset 4 with 80010000, AND at offset 13 with FFFDFFBF, and XOR at offset 22 with 00400800. Seven ordinary instructions implement pointer loading, three observed atomic loads, checksum computation and the natural RET. The complete original function remains unchanged.

The retained text is `8b442404f08108000001808b08f08120bffffdff8b10f081300008400031ca8b0031d0c3`, SHA-256 `d11040b71a34dbb05242d84500ad5df65c19340777e6b2e2673c87374e987dab`. The object has no relocations, unresolved external functions or nonempty data dependency. Its only discarded nonempty section is the original 100-byte .debug$S metadata.

`build.py` reuses `../p2-compiled-records/build.py`, pinned to SHA-256 `fe426f202b48664a87357c766d39099b9d35b5d8217c2b114696164a0d468258`. The ordinary COFF extractor changes only the function symbol and diagnostic spelling from ring3_reduce to ring3_update_flags. The permanent producer differs from the frozen discovery builder only in its repository-root depth, parents[4] instead of parents[3]. Compiler flags, tool paths, environment and complete-output extraction remain unchanged. It creates a fresh output directory and records source, tools, command argv, raw object, text and disassembly. Root performs the formal reproduction and publishes the observed artifacts. Routine integration consumes those retained bytes and does not invoke a compiler.

The planned actual proof uses one separate 37-byte authored guest caller. It invokes the complete function twice on the same live cell, preserves the first DWORD return in EBP, consumes both returns and stores their sum. Initial 00020050 gives loaded values 80030050, 80010010 and 80410810, returning 80430850. A second live call returns 80010010; the guest sum is 00440860. The caller is explicitly separate from the original compiler text. There is one declared initial CPU/RAM input and no host reseed between the two calls or retained pauses.

Four bound profiles cover replacement/resident and explicit/entry preparation. Nine original run budgets are 2/1/2/2/1/4/4/10/4. Three additional success probes distinguish full imm32 from signextended imm8, ESP/SIB displacement parsing and prefix-looking immediate payload bytes. The planned finite total is 48 runs, 132 retired instructions, 96 forwarded helpers and eight natural compiler RETs. These are source-derived expectations; observed execution and independent review belong to the evidence bank and result.json.

Existing strict V1 memory helpers, ABI records, locals, generated semantics, Read-before-Write policy, failure neutrality, MAX exhaustion and SMC behavior are reused unchanged from R3-556. This decoder-only task adds no new fault or malformed-packet matrix. The runner uses exact 4364-byte arena assertions with valid dirty FP state and selected RAM canaries. Only explicitly saved arena milestones support later whole-record review; per-run records and whole RAM are not implied to be persisted.

The claim is finite private flat32 synchronous unshared execution of this self-authored original consumer and the selected exact LOCK 81 DWORD encodings. It does not establish hardware locking, C11 concurrency or shared-memory ordering, performance, general compiler coverage or application compatibility.
